stemMd: Why does the author distinguish judging reliability from judging alerts?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To show that counting is always meaningless.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To argue that alerts cannot help reliability.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To show that different goals require different evidence.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To claim that recovery time measures message length.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To require every message to be restored.

explanationMd: Software reliability concerns actual service performance; alert quality concerns timely recognition and response. One measure cannot automatically answer both. The distinction explains the team’s use of separate outcome records.

distractorRationale.b: The questions are related, even though not identical.
distractorRationale.a: The passage criticizes one interpretation of one count.
distractorRationale.e: The revised system is not rejected.
